raw_finding.practical_consequence: A successful same-identity upsert can be reported as DIVERGENT_FINGERPRINT even when both stores received the intended content: the proposed fingerprint is computed from the input confidence before persistence, while PostgreSQL stores confidence as single-precision REAL and the exact-read path recomputes from that rounded stored value.
evidence: candidate-round-2.json#/exact_corpus_readback_contract/content_fingerprint requires `Compute once before both writes; recompute from PG stored row` and includes confidence as a stored JSON number.

src/memory_knowledge/projections/corpus_writer.py passes the input confidence into the REAL column, while src/memory_knowledge/projections/corpus_qdrant.py:31-38 passes the unrounded Python value to the projection. Values not exactly representable in REAL therefore produce different canonical JSON numbers unless the contract explicitly normalizes to stored precision or fingerprints the persisted row before Qdrant publication.
